claims.text: The initial as-cast refractory high-entropy alloy has a disordered BCC structure.
The initial as-cast alloy has a relatively coarse grain size.
Controlled aging will nucleate and grow nanoscale ordered B2 precipitates within the BCC matrix.
Optimized aging will produce a homogeneous precipitate distribution.
The nanoscale B2 precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
Dislocation pinning by the B2 precipitates will provide precipitation strengthening during high-temperature loading.
Precipitation strengthening will increase high-temperature yield strength relative to the as-cast baseline.
Precipitation strengthening will improve creep resistance relative to the as-cast baseline.
The aging treatment will increase creep rupture life relative to the as-cast baseline.
The high-temperature mechanical improvements should occur at approximately 850–900 °C under constant-load or creep conditions.
Small B2 precipitates with coherent or semi-coherent matrix interfaces will preserve room-temperature ductility.
Room-temperature mechanical properties will remain effectively unchanged after aging.
The aging treatment and associated B2 precipitation will not significantly affect overall alloy density.
A uniform precipitate distribution and optimized aging temperature and time are required to obtain the proposed benefits.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or an inhomogeneous distribution could negate the high-temperature improvement.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or an inhomogeneous distribution could degrade room-temperature performance.
